title: Privy Council Restores Barbuda Council Land Rights
reason: A Privy Council ruling on Barbuda land rights did happen in 2022, but it is the opposite of what is described. In MacKenzie Frank and another v Attorney General of Antigua and Barbuda (JCPC 2021/0070), heard 3 May 2022 and decided 13 June 2022, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council DISMISSED the Barbudans' (Trevor Walker and Mackenzie Frank) constitutional challenge to the Paradise Found (Project) Act 2015, finding it had 'no realistic prospect of succeeding' and that Barbudans hold only collective/class rights (a right to apply for a grant of occupation or grazing), not personal proprietary rights protected under the constitution. This ruling was widely described (GLAN, Antigua Observer) as 'devastating' for Barbuda, clearing the way for tourism development rather than constraining it. The event description claims the opposite outcome (ruling in favor of Barbudans, reaffirming communal tenure protections, constraining the government). A separate, later Privy Council case that did rule in Barbudans' favor (Mussington and Frank v Development Control Authority, concerning standing to challenge an airport permit on environmental/procedural grounds) was decided in February 2024, not 2022, and did not concern restoration of communal land tenure rights. No 2022 (or any-year) Privy Council ruling matches the described outcome.
